synthesized_findings: Hook policy is the parent control surface that decides when prompts, commands, and stop conditions are allowed to proceed.
The reusable doctrine is the lifecycle taxonomy and decision semantics, not the raw `.claude` folder structure.
Stop/subagent-stop hooks matter because they turn incomplete work into explicit continuation rather than silent pass-shaped output.
doctrine_implications: Represent hook classes and decisions in `contracts/hook-manifest.yaml` and `contracts/policy-decision.yaml`.
Keep allow/block/ask outcomes machine-readable so later implementations cannot hide unsafe work behind prose.
Tie hook outcomes to evaluation and promotion gates when they certify completion or deny risky behavior.
unresolved_ambiguities: The local Production Safety Constraints doc is only a title, so detailed policy behavior is currently grounded more strongly in upstream repo evidence than in local prose.
Concrete hook adapters still vary by host harness even when the doctrine is stable.
